# converge-status: show the commit date and one-line subject of the rev in the waybar tooltip

## Context

`modules/converge/` runs `cosmo-rebuild` (scripts in `modules/converge/scripts.nix`)
which converges a host to the tip of cosmo main and authors every transition to
`/var/lib/cosmo-rebuild/status` via `converge-status set`
(`pkgs/converge-status/status.go`). The waybar widget is `converge-status render`
/ `watch` (`render.go`, `watch.go`) — a pure projection of that file. Design rule
you must keep (see the header comments in `modules/converge/default.nix` and
`pkgs/converge-status/main.go`): the widget side never talks to the network and
never reconstructs state; the machinery authors everything the bar shows.

Today the tooltip shows only short SHAs:

```
classic-laddie: converged with main
deployed  b4c8d51
verified against the remote 3 minutes ago
```

The maintainer wants the commit date and the one-line commit subject alongside
the rev, e.g.

```
classic-laddie: converged with main
deployed  b4c8d51  2026-09-04 16:50  flake.lock: Update (#795)
verified against the remote 3 minutes ago
```

and likewise on the `target` line while building and the "main moved to ..."
line on failure. The bar text itself (icon + short rev) stays as it is.

## Where the metadata comes from

The script only knows the tip via `git ls-remote` (no clone anywhere; the flake
is built from `github:` tarballs, which carry no commit message). Add a bare
shallow mirror under the unit's state directory and read the metadata from it:

- `mirror="$state_dir/mirror.git"`; `git init --bare -q "$mirror"` on first use.
- Lookup for a rev: `git -C "$mirror" log -1 --format='%ct%x09%s' "$rev"`. If the
  rev is not present, do ONE `git -C "$mirror" fetch --depth=1 -q "$repo" refs/heads/main`
  and retry the log once. Both steps are best-effort: any failure yields empty
  metadata and must never change the run's exit status or the phase it records.
  Steady state (already at tip, rev already in the mirror) costs zero network;
  a rev is fetched once when first seen.
- Keep `git ls-remote` as the tip resolution exactly as it is; do not replace
  it with the fetch (its failure path is the documented "could not resolve"
  case and the tests pin it).
- Pass the result to `set` as `subject=<one line>` and `committed=<unix secs>`
  on every `set phase=building` (for `target`) and `set phase=current` (for
  `rev`) call. The "already at tip" re-observation path may look up from the
  mirror (no fetch needed if present); if it finds nothing, `set` carries the
  previous values forward (below).
- `git` is already on the unit's `path`. Nothing needs root beyond the
  StateDirectory the unit already owns.

## `converge-status` changes (`pkgs/converge-status/`)

`status.go`:
- Extend `Status` with `Subject string` and `Committed int64`; accept keys
  `subject` and `committed` in `assign`, write them in `write` (only when set).
  They describe the rev named by `identity()` (target for building/failed, rev
  for current) — document that in the schema comment on the struct.
- `set` sanitises `subject` with `oneLine(v, 120)` like `detail`.
- Carry-forward rule, alongside the existing `at` rule: if the incoming record
  has no subject/committed and `prev.identity() == next.identity()`, inherit
  prev's. Apply it AFTER the failed-phase target/deployed inheritance so an
  ExecStopPost-authored failure inherits the subject of the target it was
  building.

`render.go`:
- Add a helper that formats a rev line: short sha, then `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` in
  the host's local zone when `Committed != 0`, then the subject when present;
  omit the pieces that are absent so the old output is unchanged when no
  metadata exists (existing tests must keep passing untouched).
- Use it on: the `target` line and `deployed` line in `building`; the
  "main moved to <target>" line and `target` line in `failed`; the `deployed`
  line in `current`, the reboot views and the stale view. Metadata applies only
  to the rev it describes (identity()); do not print the target's subject on
  the deployed line or vice versa.
- Keep the relative-age lines ("started N minutes ago", "verified ... ago")
  as they are.

`main_test.go` (real-binary tests, same style as the file): add cases for
(1) set-then-render shows date and subject on the right line and only there,
(2) carry-forward on re-observed `current` and on an ExecStopPost `--unless-terminal`
failure, (3) a subject with newlines/control characters is flattened and
capped, (4) render output is byte-identical to before when no metadata is set.

## `modules/converge/scripts.nix` and `test.nix`

- Implement the mirror lookup as a small shell function in the `cosmo-rebuild`
  script (terse comments, no prose blocks). Do not add a third script.
- `test.nix` replaces `git` with a stub that currently only answers
  `ls-remote` and exits 1 otherwise. Extend the stub minimally to also answer
  `init`, `fetch`, and `log` (`-C <dir>` prefix must be tolerated), replaying a
  per-case `$CASE/commit-meta` file for `log` and a recorded exit code for
  `fetch`. Add cases: a deploy records `subject`/`committed` for the target in
  the building snapshot and for the rev in the final `current`; a mirror lookup
  that fails (fetch exit 1, log exit 1) leaves the run's phase, ledger and exit
  status exactly as the existing cases assert, with no `subject` line written.
- Update the header comments in `modules/converge/default.nix` (the sentence
  "the one ls-remote per run *is* the machine's knowledge of where main is")
  and `pkgs/converge-status/main.go` so they stay accurate: one ls-remote plus,
  on first sight of a rev, one shallow fetch into a state-dir mirror for its
  date and subject. One or two terse sentences, no more.

## Verification (ALL IN THE FOREGROUND)

```
cd pkgs/converge-status && go vet ./... && go test ./...
nix fmt && git diff --exit-code
nix build .#<the check attribute that wraps modules/converge/test.nix — find it in flake.nix> -L
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.classic-laddie.config.system.build.toplevel --dry-run
```

DO NOT run anything in the background. DO NOT use Monitor or background tasks.
Run each verification in the FOREGROUND and wait. Do not park, do not schedule
a wakeup, do not exit before committing. COMMIT AND OPEN THE PR BEFORE YOU
FINISH, and put the exact commands you ran and their results in the PR body.

## Constraints

- Code comments: extremely terse, high information density; match the density
  of the existing comments in these files. No multi-line prose blocks.
- Follow the repo's `CLAUDE.md`: no Co-Authored-By lines, no AI/LLM mention in
  commit or PR text. Branch from `main`; never commit to `main`.
- No new Go dependencies; no new flake inputs.
- Do not change the bar text, CSS classes, or the `alt`/`class` contract.
- Do not change `deployed-rev` semantics or the timers.
